app_purpose: Java network application framework (TCP/IP transport layer). Apps using ObjectSerializationCodecFactory / ObjectSerializationDecoder decode Java-native-serialized objects off the wire via org.apache.mina.core.buffer.AbstractIoBuffer#getObject(ClassLoader). After CVE-2024-52046 the decoder is default-deny: the app must accept(...) the classes it legitimately deserializes (acceptMatchers / ClassNameMatcher allowlist).
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data guarded by an INCOMPLETELY-APPLIED class-name ALLOWLIST (CWE-502). CVE-2024-52046 added the acceptMatchers allowlist (default-deny) to AbstractIoBuffer.getObject(), but enforced it ONLY in resolveClass()'s non-null branch -- i.e. for classes arriving as a MINA type-1 descriptor (write(1)+writeUTF(name)). MINA's wire format carries a per-descriptor TYPE byte and readClassDescriptor() dispatches on it; a type-0 (0x00) descriptor is routed to super.readClassDescriptor(), yielding an ObjectStreamClass whose forClass() is null, so resolveClass() takes its null-clazz branch -- which calls Class.forName(name, false, classLoader) with NO acceptMatchers consultation. An attacker controls the wire bytes and can wrap any non-allowlisted class in a 0x00 type-0 descriptor to bypass the allowlist entirely (the object is then fully reconstructed, running readObject). CVE-2026-42779 closes this in 2.2.7 by hoisting the acceptMatchers check ahead of every Class.forName in resolveClass() (covering the null-clazz branch) and readClassDescriptor().
external_trigger_note: Apache MINA is a NETWORK framework, not an HTTP app: its real entry point is a TCP server. The trigger is a REAL EXTERNAL network trigger -- a separate `client` container (Client.java) connects over TCP across the docker network to a REAL MINA NioSocketAcceptor + ProtocolCodecFilter(ObjectSerializationCodecFactory) server (Server.java) and writes the crafted length-prefixed MINA serialized stream. The server's REAL, unmodified published mina-core decoder (doDecode -> in.setMatchers(acceptMatchers) -> in.getObject(classLoader)) deserializes it through the real allowlist. Not HTTP, but a genuine external TCP network trigger, which is exactly how MINA is used in production and satisfies the external-trigger requirement for a network framework. Nothing is deserialized in-process by a test harness.

flag.resource: the class-deserialization allowlist (acceptMatchers/ClassNameMatcher, default-deny) that CVE-2024-52046 added to AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() to keep untrusted classes from being deserialized/loaded; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir that only a class reconstructed past that guard can read
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) in the SERVER container at start. PcbSeed.readObject() reads that file into its transient `flag` field during server-side reconstruction; the server IoHandler then echoes the token back over the SAME TCP connection. Absent from MINA source, Server.java, Client.java. The external client NEVER holds the canary: the serialized stream it sends carries only class name + descriptor + empty field data (the flag field is transient).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2024-52046: the ObjectSerializationDecoder / AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() lacked deserialization defenses; the fix (2.0.27/2.1.10/2.2.4) added the acceptMatchers/ClassNameMatcher allowlist (accept(Class...)/accept(Pattern)/accept(String...)), default-deny, enforced in resolveClass()'s non-null branch. CVE-2026-41635: the type-0/null-clazz descriptor branch of resolveClass() does NOT consult the allowlist, reaching Class.forName(); fixed on mainline but not backported to 2.1.x/2.2.x. CVE-2026-42779: 'an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-41635' -- a 0x00 type-0 descriptor still reaches Class.forName() without acceptMatchers on the 2.2.x line, fixed in 2.2.7 by hoisting the allowlist check ahead of every Class.forName in resolveClass() (both branches) and readClassDescriptor(). SOURCE-VERIFIED from Maven Central sources jars: AbstractIoBuffer.java is byte-identical 2.2.5==2.2.6; 2.2.6->2.2.7 changes only AbstractIoBuffer.java; 2.2.3 has no allowlist.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 as REAL-SERVER-TCP (hard policy: the prior in-process Driver.getObject() trigger was BANNED). Apache MINA is a NETWORK framework, so each version now runs a REAL MINA NioSocketAcceptor TCP server (app/Server.java) with ProtocolCodecFilter(new ObjectSerializationCodecFactory()) and the acceptMatchers allowlist configured (via reflection, so one source compiles on V0=2.2.3 which predates the accept() API) to accept ONLY the legit class PcbExpected -- NOT PcbSeed. A SEPARATE `client` container (app/Client.java) connects over TCP across the docker network and writes the crafted length-prefixed MINA serialized stream; the server's REAL, unmodified published mina-core decoder path (ObjectSerializationDecoder.doDecode -> in.setMatchers(acceptMatchers) -> AbstractIoBuffer.getObject(ClassLoader)) deserializes it through the real allowlist. Genuine EXTERNAL network trigger (real TCP, separate process/container) -- the way MINA is actually used; not HTTP but a real network entry point. No MINA code edited. Runtime = maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-11, REAL Maven Central mina-core 2.2.3/2.2.6/2.2.7. Variant A (same running sink getObject(); same canary CLASS PcbSeed; same rce-oob channel /canary/flag.txt read in readObject, echoed back over the SAME TCP connection by the IoHandler). The ONLY difference between the original seed and the residual is the MINA WIRE DESCRIPTOR TYPE: original = normal type-1 (write(1)+writeUTF, allowlist-checked in resolveClass's non-null branch); residual = forced type-0/null-clazz (0x00 + standard Java descriptor, routed to resolveClass's null-clazz branch). GUARD lineage source-verified from upstream sources jars: V0=2.2.3 has NO allowlist API (resolveClass returns any class); V1=2.2.6 has the CVE-2024-52046 acceptMatchers allowlist enforced ONLY in resolveClass's non-null (type-1) branch (null-clazz/type-0 branch = Class.forName(name,false) with no allowlist) and is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 2.2.5 (the CVE-2026-41635 fix never backported to 2.2.x); V2=2.2.7 is the CVE-2026-42779 fix -- resolveClass applies acceptMatchers before any Class.forName for BOTH branches (readClassDescriptor's type-1 path likewise). BENIGN benchmark canary (rce-oob): PcbSeed reads /canary/flag.txt only in readObject(); flag field is transient (never on the wire); no gadget chain, no JNDI/RMI, no command execution. The client generates the MINA streams itself at runtime (pure java.io, no canary present), so they carry only class name + descriptor + empty field data, never the flag. RUNTIME REPRODUCED over real external TCP (flag=PCBFLAG_fb2c8a17394a5219cc646385b2a08400): original(PcbSeed type-1)@v0 -> server echoes PCB_SEED_FLAG=<flag> (reaches; no accept() API); original(type-1)@v1 -> PCB_BLOCKED=ClassNotFoundException, no flag (allowlist blocks in resolveClass non-null branch); expected(PcbExpected type-1)@v1 -> PCB_OK=PcbExpected (allowlist is LIVE, not deny-all); bypass(PcbSeed type-0)@v1 -> server echoes PCB_SEED_FLAG=<flag> (residual reaches PAST the allowlist via the null-clazz branch); bypass(type-0)@v2 -> PCB_BLOCKED='Class not in accept list PcbSeed', no flag; original(type-1)@v2 -> PCB_BLOCKED='Class not in accept list PcbSeed', no flag. KEY: on the SAME v1 (2.2.6) server, type-1 PcbSeed is BLOCKED while the byte-identical type-0-wrapped PcbSeed REACHES -- directly demonstrating the incomplete allowlist over a real network trigger. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct releases (2.2.3->2.2.6->2.2.7); V1 genuinely has the -52046 guard (type-1 seed IS rejected, PcbExpected accepted) and is genuinely bypassed by the type-0 residual it does not cover; V2 closes exactly that residual; original != residual on V1 (type-1 BLOCKED vs type-0 REACHES); V1 does NOT block the residual (2.2.6 does not already block type-0). LITERAL 41635->42779 / 2.2.5->2.2.6->2.2.7 3-version framing refuted (2.2.5==2.2.6 => V1==V0, fixes collapse to 2.2.7); rebuilt as 52046->42779 with V0=2.2.3 exercising the SAME type-0/null-clazz mechanism (see cve_pair.note_on_literal_41635_42779_pair).
